Headteacher's Welcome
Our vision is simple, we are a staff body committed to our students with an emphasis on ambition, respect and our academy’s community.
Stanchester Academy is well known for its welcoming atmosphere built on the strong relationships between staff and students. Our academic approach is for every student to enjoy learning. We strive to ensure that our teaching standards are high, children feel safe and supported in school, and that our lessons follow a knowledge-rich and rigorous curriculum.
At Stanchester Academy we have an exceptional team of dedicated staff who provide an inspiring and supportive learning environment. As educators, our core purpose is to ensure that every student is challenged to realise their full potential and encouraged to be aspirational in their choices for the future.
As a result of high-quality teaching, students make clear progress towards subject mastery, and can articulate their areas for development confidently. There is a culture of self-improvement in which both staff and students continually seek to learn and improve. Stanchester Academy aspires to ensure there is no wasted time, and for every child to have purpose, come prepared, and feel proud.

School Vision
Stanchester Academy is a community built on the values of mutual respect and ambition for everyone.
Our aim is to cultivate a vibrant and inclusive community that values respect, fosters a sense of belonging, and empowers individuals to achieve their highest potential.
We strive to be a school where respect is the foundation of all interactions, where students, teachers, staff, and parents treat one another with dignity, empathy, and kindness. In our community, diversity is celebrated, and every voice is heard and respected, creating an environment where everyone feels valued and supported.
Through a strong sense of community, we aim to create lasting connections among students, teachers, staff, and families. We believe that collaboration and cooperation are key to building a nurturing and cohesive environment, where everyone feels a sense of belonging and actively contributes to the collective success of our school.

Careers Programme Information
Our aim at Stanchester Academy is for all students to achieve their personal best. In careers education, this translates as every student making well-informed decisions about their future.
Stanchester Careers will:
Careers Education: delivered through the tutor programme, curriculum, and PSHRE to give students the knowledge and skills to make confident choices
Watch a walk through video of our careers pages here.
Autumn-Careers-Calendar-26-27.pdf
Watch a walk through of our careers calendar here.
At Stanchester Academy, we focus on 8 key 'Employability Skills'. These skills are embedded in all lessons to make explicit links between student learning and their futures.

Our PSHE / Careers and Citizenship Curriculum, ensures that the key skills and essential knowledge permeate our curriculum from year 7 to year 11, allowing our pupils to make links in their learning as well as develop the ability to think more deeply about what they are learning.
All teachers include careers into their lessons and develop student’s employability skills. Staff have access to a wide range of resources on the school Intranet to showcase careers in their subject lessons.
Teachers are encouraged to implement the below into the curriculum:
At Stanchester Academy we demonstrate the impact of our careers programme by evaluating how our careers provision influences our students’ knowledge, skills, aspirations, confidence and future destinations.
We use student surveys, questionnaires and focus groups to identify changes in students’ understanding of different careers, pathways and the skills required for employment. Feedback from students, parents, teachers, employers and other partners also shows whether careers activities are relevant, accessible and meeting students’ needs.
The impact of individual careers activities is shown through student reflections, participation data and evidence of changes in knowledge or confidence. As a school we track engagement with careers guidance, work experience, employer encounters, further education and apprenticeship providers, and other careers-related opportunities through the use of Compass+ and Arbor.
Longer-term impact is demonstrated through destination data, including our students’ progression into further education, apprenticeships, employment or training. We analyse this information by year group and, where appropriate, identify differences between groups of students to ensure that careers provision is supporting all learners and addressing potential gaps.
We then bring this evidence together through regular evaluation and use the findings to improve our careers programme, using a clear cycle of plan → deliver → measure impact → evaluate → improve, demonstrating not simply what careers activities have taken place, but how they have contributed to better-informed and more confident decisions about students’ futures.

Our Personal Development lessons have been designed to increase student knowledge around thinking ahead to their futures. We introduce students to the options process in Year 8, allowing them time to look into the GCSE options available at Stanchester (subject to change), but also the sorts of courses and apprenticeships available post 16 and what the entry requirements are for these courses. This then allows students to further consider the subjects to study at GCSE that may link to their future careers and courses of interest. Please take a look at the Year 9 Options area of our website for more information. You will also find some more support here: Choosing Options

Reporting and Assessment
Three times during the academic year students will receive a progress report (PR1, 2 and 3). Each report contains a summary of assessment data in each subject, along with a teacher assessed grading on a student’s attitude to learning (ATL) and behaviour for learning (BFL) in class. Where a student receives an ATL or BFL score of a 3 or lower, teachers will note a ‘Area to Improve Most’ (AIM) which follows the code below.
For KS3, each report will contain an average knowledge assessment score from across the term along with end of year assessment scores on PR3. For subjects that primarily assess skills (PE, Art, DT, Drama, Music) they have a bespoke 1-5 skills grading each term. Details for each subject can be found below.
PE KS3 Skills Grading Criteria
Art/DT KS3 Skills Grading Criteria
Drama/Music Skills Grading Criteria
For KS4, each report will contain assessment scores or mock exams grades along with a prediction for the end of year based on assessment data and attitude to learning.

Uniform
Uniform is an important part of a school’s identity. It reinforces who we are as a community and helps allow students to feel pride in their school. It also ensures students are not put under any pressure because of the type of clothes they wear and all are treated equally. It also helps prepare students for life after school where many will have to dress smartly for work.
We expect all students to be in correct uniform at all times. We also want to support you in buying affordable, good quality clothing for school which your children accept they have to wear because the rules are very clear. We want to make it easier for parents and help reduce any issues there may be over what is and isn’t acceptable uniform. If you want to buy uniform from another store or online, that is acceptable, but it must match the uniform on the guidance below exactly, making the process of getting the right uniform even easier.

Reading for Pleasure
At Stanchester, we recognise the power of Reading for Pleasure and developing pupils into lifelong readers. All KS3 pupils have 2-3 Reading for Pleasure sessions during their morning tutor time in which they read a book as a group from the selection below. These sessions are designed to give students the opportunity to spend time reading a shared class text, and texts are selected by class discussion and democratic vote.
Our Reading for Pleasure curriculum is both a window and a mirror: each option is carefully selected to allow students to hold a mirror up to their own selves through the rich and wonderful texts that we read, while also reflecting upon their own thoughts, feelings, and place within the world. Thus, these texts become a window out into the world of wider human experiences, different customs and beliefs as well as new and enriching knowledge which will only unlock more windows and doors for them in the future.

Curriculum Overview
At Stanchester Academy we aim to offer students a curriculum that equips them with the knowledge and skills to successfully progress onto further education and ultimately into employment of their choice. We operate a two-week timetable with 25 periods per week distributed across a range of subjects as seen below. Alongside our ‘timetabled curriculum’, we offer a ‘wider curriculum’ that includes our daily tutor time sessions, enrichment activities, sports clubs, STEM, and careers programmes alongside much more.
Key Stage 3
In key stage 3 we offer a broad range of subjects that are carefully balanced to ensure that all students develop knowledge and skills across different subject disciplines. Across Years 7 to 9 students study our bespoke Business and Digital Skills course that equips them with applied computing knowledge, an insight into the world of business and employment, alongside valuable careers, and enterprise-based skills. In Years 7 and 8, a new lesson specifically for PSHE has been introduced that will be expanded across KS3 and KS4 next year.
Key Stage 4
Students begin studying their GCSE Maths and Science towards the end of Year 9. However, Year 10 serves as the formal start to GCSE studies and requires students to select their option subjects from a curated list of subjects. In Years 10 and 11 timetables follow the allocations below. We have purposefully ensured that Year 10 and 11 students receive 2 lessons of PE a week for the benefit of their physical and mental wellbeing.
